common_name: Australasian Montium-Subgroup Fly (Cuticular Hydrocarbon & Tergite Clines)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila serrata (2.1 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.what_changes: At fixed activator diffusivity, raising the inhibitor:activator ratio δ shortens the detail-scale critical wavelength from 2134 nm (sechellia, 1.025× onset) through 2123 nm (serrata, Holocene, 1.085× onset) to 2102 nm (silvestris, 1.220× onset). The 0 Ma serrata state is the intermediate wavenumber, not a copy of either neighbor. A separate 92 µm cellular-tier slot for this species is not reused.

equations.activator: du/dt = Du * laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v
equations.inhibitor: dv/dt = Dv * laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv fu + Du gv) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.radial_ocellus: linear critical mode on the disk is proportional to J0(k_c r)

parameters.note: Du is solved so that k_c(delta_serrata) = 2 pi / 2.123e-6 m. Neighbor wavelengths use that same Du.

boundary_conditions.patch: periodic square of side 8 * lambda_serrata for the tergite micro-patch
boundary_conditions.ocellus: radial disk mode J0(k_c r) with a weak anterior-posterior cosine anisotropy
boundary_conditions.equal_diffusion_control: Dv = Du, same kinetics, linearly stable

empirical_claims.claim: D. serrata cuticular hydrocarbons differ from D. birchii and function in mate choice.
Natural selection on CHCs reinforces mate recognition between D. serrata and D. birchii.
CHC profiles form latitudinal clines in D. serrata along the Australian east coast.
A two-species reaction-diffusion system selects a finite critical wavenumber when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion relation and diffusion-driven instability
D. serrata CHC identity, mate choice, and an east-coast latitudinal CHC cline
reconstructed_in_script: Assignment of the MorphoEval detail scale 2.123e-6 m as lambda_c
Chronoseries ordering sechellia 2134 nm > serrata 2123 nm > silvestris 2102 nm at fixed Du
Latitude slope 0.012 mapping the CHC cline direction onto delta
transfer_boundary: Gallery plate is a project micrograph-style fallback, not a measured 2.1 µm electron micrograph
GIF color palette is the specimen luminance-quantile RGB table, not a pixel copy of the photograph
does_not_claim: That a published paper measured an ocellar Turing wavelength of 2.123 µm in D. serrata
That D. sechellia is the phylogenetic sister of D. serrata (it is the chronoseries predecessor only)
That the equal-diffusion control produces spots
